title: docs(guide): remove the lazy-loading promise nothing keeps from the schema-rendering guide (objectui#9989)
body:
Fixes #9989

Clause-②: no — a documentation page. It moves no exported symbol and no key on a published payload.

One file: `content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md`. Nothing outside `content/docs/**` is edited.

## The card's one un-taken claim, re-taken here

The card relayed, without re-running it, that the published example is refused with `invalid_type` at path `["items"]`. **Re-measured first-hand against the BUILT `TabsSchema`** (`packages/types` built in this worktree, imported through the package's own `./zod` export condition, i.e. `dist/zod/index.zod.js` — the surface a reader imports), reading the fence out of the file in the same command that measured it:

```
FILE STATE (same command): content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md
  sha256 = e726e2985330081c788a5e42ba387cefa4ce9305fbc0fdcedf0cdd8d6b19f8ab

--- STAGE 1: JSON.parse of the fence exactly as published
  JSON.parse: THROWS -> Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 86 (line 5 column 35)
  CONTROL, same command: the same bytes with the two comment spans removed
  CONTROL JSON.parse: OK  <= so the comment IS the parse fault, not some other byte

--- STAGE 2: CARD-CLAIM re-take -- TabsSchema.safeParse(the node, comments removed)
  success = false
    issue: code=invalid_type path=["items"] message="Invalid input: expected array, received undefined" expected=array
  CONTROL, same command: the SAME node with `tabs` respelled `items` and each item given value/label/content
  CONTROL success = true  <= the instrument accepts a well-formed tabs node, so the refusal is about THIS node
```

⇒ **The card's claim stands, verbatim.** Two corrections to the reasoning around it, both first-hand:

1. **The node face does NOT strip.** The card says "the face strips what it does not declare". `TabsSchema` extends `BaseSchema`, and `BaseSchemaCore` ends `.passthrough()`, which `.extend()` carries through. Measured: a correct node plus `lazyLoad` plus `tabs` parses green and the surviving keys are `["type","defaultValue","items","lazyLoad","tabs"]` — **both undeclared keys survive**. The strip is real one level down: `TabItemSchema` is a plain object, and `{value,label,content,title,body}` comes back as `["value","label","content"]`. The empty-tab-bar outcome the card predicts is right; it arrives because `items` is absent, not because anything was stripped off the node.
2. **The card's three-row key table is not sufficient on its own.** Applying it literally — `title` to `label`, `body` to `content` — still fails, because `TabItemSchema` requires `value` too: `invalid_type@["items",0,"value"]` and `["items",1,"value"]`, plus `invalid_union@[…,"content"]` for a `content` that is not a node. Adding `value` turns it green. The doc now teaches all three required item keys.

## Which route I took on the `lazyLoad` promise, and the measurement that decided it

**Route taken: nothing lazy-loads tab bodies ⇒ the promise is removed, not respelled.** The sentence "Large schemas are automatically optimized:" and its example are gone. Four readings, each with a same-subject control in the same command:

| measurement | reading | control, same command |
|:--|:--|:--|
| schemas in the built `zod` barrel declaring `lazyLoad` | **0** | `defaultValue` on **17** of them |
| reads of `.lazyLoad` anywhere in the repository | **2**, both inside `usePerformance.ts` itself (the defaulting expression and the memo dependency) | `debounceMs` is also lifted into a local and handed to `setTimeout` — `lazyLoad` has no such line |
| the one caller, `apps/console/src/components/PerformanceDashboard.tsx` | calls `usePerformance()` with **no argument**; reads `lazyLoad` **0** times and `perf.config.` **0** times | it reads `metrics` 15 times, so the file does use the hook's result |
| the `tabs` renderer | `lazyLoad` **0** lines, `React.lazy` **0**, `Suspense` **0**, `usePerformance` **0**; `schema.items` mapped on **2** lines, unconditionally — triggers and panels | `defaultValue` on **3** lines — the card's own control, a key this renderer really reads |

⇒ `lazyLoad` is inert even on the surface it genuinely belongs to: `usePerformance` resolves it into the config object it returns and never branches on it, and no caller reads it back. And there is no lazy gate on the tabs path to point it at even if it were live. So correcting the keys while leaving the sentence would have been, in the card's words, the same defect with better spelling.

**Whether a corrected `tabs` example belongs in its place — I kept one, deliberately.** The harm this card names has two halves: a false promise, and four wrong key spellings sitting at a well-trafficked address. Deleting the block repairs the first and abandons the second. The replacement keeps a correct `tabs` node where the wrong one stood, labelled `For reference` rather than as an optimization, and states the two failure modes an author actually meets — measured, not asserted:

- an item missing `value`, `label` or `content` is **refused** (`invalid_type` at that path — measured for all three);
- an item that also carries `title` / `body` is **accepted with those keys dropped**, so the panel renders empty with nothing naming the cause;
- on the node itself `body` and `children` are refused **by name**, by the ADR-0049 tombstones already in `TabsSchema`.

The section now points deferral work at `Code Splitting`, the mechanism further down the same page that does exist.

## The invalid-JSON half, and why no gate caught it

The old fence was tagged `json` and carried a block comment, so a copy failed to parse before reaching the schema. After this change **every one of the 13 `json` fences on this page parses**, checked by `JSON.parse` in the same command that hashed the file, with a deliberately broken literal as the instrument control. The replacement node also `safeParse`s green against the built `TabsSchema`, with the pre-fix node re-parsed by the same instrument as the negative control.

**Why no gate caught it — measured, ⛔ not fixed here (out of scope by the dispatch order):** no gate in this repository asserts that a `json`-tagged fence is valid JSON.

- `check:doc-snippets` compiles `ts` / `tsx` / `typescript` only. Its own header: a json fence is never compiled against anything.
- `check:doc-fences` asks whether a **TypeScript body** sits under a non-TypeScript fence. A JSON body under a `json` fence is exactly right by its classifier.
- `check:doc-types` judges the `type` literal and, in its own words, deliberately not the snippet's other keys.
- `check:doc-expression-carriage` is the only gate that reads json fence bodies — and it is **report-only**, and its tolerance list removes line and block comments and re-escapes raw newlines **before** parsing. So the two shapes that make a fence uncopyable are normalized away by design. It printed `225 json/jsonc fence(s), 225 parsed, 0 UNPARSED` on this tree.

Population reading, taken here for the record: **22 of 199 `json` fences under `content/docs` are rejected by `JSON.parse`** (control: the same parser rejects a trailing-comma literal, so the count is a reading). Several are deliberate — elision markers and `// Bad:` counter-examples — which is precisely why deciding the class is a triage call and not a drive-by widening of this PR. Reported for filing; `#9941` is not addressed here either.

Tests that read this page, run from the repo root: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/components/src/__tests__/guide-schema-rendering-data-context-8021.test.tsx scripts/__tests__/check-doc-component-types.test.ts` — **2 files, 132 tests passed**.

**Changeset: none owed, decided by running the gate rather than from memory.** `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — "1 file(s) changed, 0 of them published source of a package the release covers, 0 of them a manifest whose published contract moved … no changeset is owed."

**Ablation, proving the link gate really judges the new in-page anchor** (the `Code Splitting` reference is a new link, so its green needed to be a reading). Mutation and restore both proved by object hash against the HEAD blob, ⛔ never by an exit code, with the mutation script refusing on an anchor miss and restoring from a `trap`:

```
HEAD blob   = c79d152981943f7cb72d2d12160d31f973899c6e
on-disk pre = c79d152981943f7cb72d2d12160d31f973899c6e
MUTATE -> removed text grep -c = 0 · injected text grep -c = 1 · hash = 4ef714ff4394cccd1548e93b18d73be48cb8323d
  gate on MUTATED tree: exit 1
  "[anchor] content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md:363 -> #no-such-heading-on-this-page"
RESTORE (git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH)
  on-disk post-restore hash = c79d152981943f7cb72d2d12160d31f973899c6e  equals HEAD blob? YES
  injected grep -c = 0 · original grep -c = 1 · git diff HEAD empty? YES
  gate on RESTORED tree: exit 0
```

Repository-wide scans (`pnpm lint`, the full `pnpm test`) are CI's run, not owed here; this diff touches no JavaScript or TypeScript source.

## Acceptance notes

Seen while measuring, ⛔ not filed and ⛔ not repaired here:

- **noted, not filed** — the `tabs` renderer reads `item.content` with a tolerant fallback to a cast `item.body`. It is unreachable through the published face, which strips `body` off an item before the renderer sees it, so it only fires on a document that was never parsed. Successor who touches it: the next change to `TabsSchema`'s item shape. Contract-first says a fix belongs on the producer side, ⛔ not in the consumer's fallback, and the producer here is already correct.
- **noted, not filed** — the sibling `Memoization` subsection on this page asserts "the renderer automatically memoizes components". No measurement of that was taken in this act, in either direction; it is named so the next reader knows it is unmeasured rather than checked. Successor who touches it: whoever takes the `json`-fence class below, since it is the same page.
